title: Vendor Portal: AI panel cannot be closed by keyboard once it has focus
product: @vc-shell/framework / Marketplace Vendor Portal (separate product, not the storefront)

half_1_vc_shell: PR #292 (46098e500) — adds the CLOSE_PANEL message to the chat->shell protocol; in v2.5.0, not v2.4.0

PR #305 (9aea3dee3) — validates event.source (the registered iframe's contentWindow), not just event.origin; in v2.5.0, not v2.4.0. A real security fix: previously ANY window at an allowed origin could close the panel.
two_halves_two_repos.half_2_virto_oz: VirtoCommerce/virto-oz#17 — the chat app forwards its own Escape / Ctrl+I as window.parent.postMessage({type:'CLOSE_PANEL'}, <shell origin>). Created 2026-08-18, CLOSED stateReason=COMPLETED 2026-08-20.
two_halves_two_repos.why_testable_now: On 2026-08-12 the fix author asked QA explicitly NOT to retest before half 2 shipped ('rather than retesting against the shell build and finding it unchanged'). That was correct then. virto-oz#17 closed COMPLETED 08-20, the deployed build is 08-24, and the panel is a SEPARATELY deployed app whose half does not depend on the vendor-portal build date. This run was on time, not premature.
two_halves_two_repos.structural_root_cause: A keystroke is delivered to the document owning the focused element; the panel is a cross-origin iframe; a cross-origin parent cannot observe those events by any means. It needed a relay, not a better listener.
two_halves_two_repos.ticket_premise_corrected: The ticket says 'the iframe capturing focus is correct for a11y', implying the shell focuses it. It does not — there is no focus() call anywhere in the ai-agent plugin. The CHAT autofocuses its own input on load.

check3_host_side_path_regression.method_note: deliberately clicked a NEUTRAL non-input target (the '1-20 of 466' pagination label) rather than the blade's search box, so Escape could not be swallowed by an input and confound the result

check4_shift_tab_workaround.result: real Shift+Tab presses walked back from the auto-focused chat input through the suggestion buttons and 'Chat history' to 'New chat' (the chat's first focusable element); one further Shift+Tab LEFT the iframe and landed on button 'Close' [active], computed accessible name exactly 'Close'. Not merely reachable but ACTIONABLE — Enter on it closed the panel, blade intact.

check5_console.verdict: clean (corroboration, not the diagnostic it would have been on a failure)
check5_console.result: 0 errors, 2 warnings across the run, and NOT ONE console entry emitted by any Ctrl+I / Escape / Shift+Tab press — all messages were page-load lines. Closes were immediate, no polling or timeout smell.

why_half_2_is_proven_live: A cross-origin parent physically cannot observe keystrokes delivered to the iframe's document. Yet the panel closed on Escape AND on Ctrl+I while the host's activeElement was that iframe. The only mechanism that can produce that is the chat app's CLOSE_PANEL postMessage reaching the shell — so the deployed virto-oz app IS forwarding, and #305's event.source validation IS accepting it (the message arrives from the chat's top-level window, as #305 requires). Nothing was rejected as an unexpected sender.
notes: The Shift+Tab workaround the author asked to have recorded does work — but the Close button's tooltip ALREADY ships an 'Esc' key badge, so the UI itself advertises Escape. Worth saying that when recording the workaround, rather than presenting Shift+Tab as the route of last resort.

Load-time warning, not a defect: '[@vc-shell/framework#ai-agent-context] Cannot set context data: no blade id available' fires at page load BEFORE the panel is opened, and the panel then worked correctly every time. Low signal; noted because it recurred across several runs today.

RESOLVED — the previously-reported environment 500s are STALE CONSOLE HISTORY, not live failures. Surfacing the full console showed 500s (security/seller/users/search, .../create, seller/offers, message/unreadcount, conversation/search, validatepasswordresettoken), SignalR 401s and a 'signIn failed: SessionExpiredError' ALL timestamped 12:34-12:36Z, predating this run's 14:52Z navigation — leftover history from an earlier session in the same browser profile. This settles a question that recurred across several tickets today: that 'known env noise' list was never a stable property of vcmp-dev, and console-derived findings on this lane must be timestamp-checked against the run window before being attributed. The one genuinely in-window error was 'WebSocket closed with status code: 1006' on pushNotificationHub at 14:56:18 — known SignalR noise, unrelated to the AI panel.
